note: Each coverage row names the rule that DISCHARGES the criterion, not merely a rule in the same area - the Major finding D2's review raised and D3 avoided. TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS, both verified by reading .claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-traceability.ts rather than inferred. (1) The sensor resolves a functional-design unit's upstream set by intersecting the ACs in THIS record's inception/user-stories/stories.md with the stories the story map maps to this unit (lines 472-495). D4's stories are US3.x and US4.x, which exist ONLY in the prior record 261016-shikhokplus-tuition-app; this record's stories.md carries US1.x and US2.x. So the derivable set is EMPTY and the sensor emits the reason 'stories mapped to unit teaching-and-recording contain no acceptance-criterion IDs', which counts one finding whatever this file says. D3 did not hit this because US1.14 is in both records. upstream_ids below enumerates the 40 REAL prior-record ACs rather than the empty derivable set, because the alternative is a file that satisfies a sensor and records nothing. (2) The story map's US3.x/US4.x row TITLES do not match the prior record's stories - it lists US3.6, US4.5, US4.6 and US4.7, which exist in neither record, and names US3.1 as recurrence where the prior record's US3.1 is the mid-class path and recurrence is US3.0. The ACs that exist are what is traced. BR ids are unit-scoped, as in D1, D2 and D3, so D4 numbers from BR1.1. The reverse array explains twelve rules that implement a system-wide constraint, a project rule or an upstream FR with no acceptance criterion of its own.

coverage.target: A pre-submit confirmation naming the present and absent counts. It is a screen behaviour with no server rule: the counts are derived from the roster the client already holds, and no response schema or business rule changes. Specified at the mockups and built in this unit's Compose work.

reverse.target: The conditional-update mechanism. Implements FR11.4, FR11.5 and ADR-006, whose contract-level specification is contract-summary.md B.8. No acceptance criterion states it, because US3.1 predates the queue - AC3.1.3 was added at Refined Mockups and the concurrency rule at Domain Design.

The concurrency guarantee: of N racing writes exactly one applies and N-1 conflict. Derived from ADR-006 and from the team Testing Posture rule that idempotency and race guarantees are tested concurrently and never sequentially. No AC, because no story describes two devices.
Re-apply carries a fresh client_mutation_id. From contract-summary.md B.7 and B.8, which call it a non-obvious consequence worth stating. No AC: the conflict state itself postdates US3.1.
A replayed client_mutation_id returns the original and writes nothing. Implements contract-summary.md B.7, which cites AC9.2.4 - a criterion belonging to US9, which is not mapped to this unit.
The four queue states never appear in a response schema. A contract constraint from B.8, protecting against a field the server cannot know the value of. No AC describes an absence of a field.
The error code, its class and the authorization-before-conflict ordering. Implements the existence-oracle rule in app/errors/codes.py and NFR14.3, both system-wide.
Interactive writes carry no version and cannot conflict. Implements FR11.4's first half. Stated so the queued-path rule does not spread to every write in the unit.
Every route resolves a lens. The project-wide MANDATED rule [TC-11, D-2], enforced by the built route-enumeration test. Applies to every unit and has no AC of its own.

No teacher-facing response carries an owner-private profile field or a global account id. The system-wide privacy invariant [TC-13, D-5, ADR-001], enforced by the built gate in app/contract/privacy.py.
An inactive batch is read-only. Follows from Batch.active, which is built and whose docstring states the semantic. No AC in US3 or US4 names it, because batch deactivation belongs to US2.

A disposition and a retention class for each of the six new tables. The standing per-unit obligation from unit-of-work.md, enforced by tests/db/test_governance.py. The values are transcribed from the prior components catalogue.
A per-screen row in docs/delivery/bangla-layout-check.md for each of this unit's seven screens. The standing per-unit obligation [FR0.2, TC-15, D-43].
